newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Oppn says Telstra profit too high for sale.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Oppn says Telstra profit too high for sale.

text.p: The Australian Opposition said on Friday Telstra Corp's 35 net profit rise in 1995/96 proved the state-owned telecommunications carrier should not be sold.
Earlier, Telstra posted a net profit of A$2.3 billion for the year to June 30, up from A$1.75 billion previously.

"This is proof that Telstra is a highly successful Australian company, which pays enormous monies into public revenue," opposition communications spokesman Chris Schacht said in a statement. "The Australian public is benefiting from not only the dividend paid by Telstra, but from owning an appreciating asset."
Telstra said it would pay a total dividend of A$1.368 billion for 1995/96, up 20 percent compared to the previous year.
The government plans to raise A$8.0 billion through the sale of one-third of Telstra.
A non-government senate committee recommended against the sale earlier this week, saying it did not find any evidence that it would be beneficial.
The opposition Labor Party and the Australian Democrats both oppose the partial privatisation, leaving Telstra's fate in the hands of independent senators Brian Harradine and Mal Colston.
